title: Hosted API: Quality Tiers PRD with Stepwise Scope Reduction and Launch Runbook
creator: Priya Raman
description: Summary: Deliver a formal PRD and launch runbook that introduces configurable quality tiers (Gold / Standard / Economy) for hosted generation and embeddings endpoints. Quality tiers are a lightweight way for customers to trade off latency, cost, and consistency without requiring model switching. This ticket defines product requirements, operational acceptance, staged scope reduction (a deliberate plan to narrow features if readiness criteria fail), and a prescriptive launch checklist for self-serve and enterprise flows.
scope_changes:
Scope v1 (target): - Expose 'quality_tier' on create call for completions/chat and embeddings. - Implement server-side routing to tuned runtime profiles (e.g., batching aggressiveness, KV cache TTLs, quantization preference) mapped to tiers. - Console UI: toggle and per-route defaults. - Telemetry: per-tier latency/cost/quality metrics and canary alerting. - Backwards compatibility: default maps to 'Standard'.

If any critical engineering readiness gates fail, the approved scope reduction plan is: Step A: Remove console UI and gate tiers to API-only (admin flag). Step B: Disable Economy tier and continue Gold/Standard. Step C: Launch with Standard-only and enable feature-flag for tier rollout. Each step includes specific rollout and communication tasks in the runbook. This stepwise scope-reduction is mandatory for go/no-go decisions during staging.
requirements:
Functional requirements: 1) API: request param 'quality_tier' with enum [gold,standard,economy] and documented semantic meaning. 2) Runtime: three preset profiles that map to kernel selection, aggressive batching windows, KV cache TTL, and optional post-filtering budget for hallucination mitigation. 3) SDKs: default enum mapping preserved across SDK languages. 4) Console: route-level default and account-level override with explanation of tradeoffs. 5) Billing: per-token multiplier metadata emitted into billing pipeline. 6) Telemetry: tagged traces and metrics for each tier, and per-tier sampling of prompts/outputs for quality evaluation.

Non-functional requirements: 1) Gold latency P95 <= 450ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) in us-west region under baseline traffic. 2) Standard latency P95 <= 300ms. Economy latency P95 <= 600ms but optimized for cost. 3) No regression to existing endpoints when 'quality_tier' omitted. 4) Security: no sensitive customer data exported to telemetry; all samples must be opt-out and sampled via customer-specific flags.

Operational requirements: - Must include canary circuit-breaker that automatically falls back to Standard if Gold path exceeds error threshold for 5 minutes. - Must support manual account-level lockdown in Console. - Must generate daily data for eval pipeline comparing per-tier quality against baseline prompts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) API spec published and SDKs updated with example in the README. 2) End-to-end test harness demonstrates three tiers with deterministic routing to runtime profiles. 3) Synthetic workload: per-tier latency and cost metrics collected in staging matching NFRs for 72h. 4) Console: ability to set route default and override at account level verified in UX smoke tests. 5) Billing pipeline emits 'tier_multiplier' and charges reflect expected unit economics in a billing sandbox. 6) Rollout gating: canary plan successfully moves 1% -> 5% -> 25% traffic with automated rollback on error rate or quality regression. 7) Security review signed off and sampling opt-out confirmed. 8) Documentation: PRD, runbook, and customer-facing doc published and linked from SDK quickstart.

Edge acceptance items (if shipping Economy): - Quality evaluation shows economy tier preserves basic intent correctness >= 85% on acceptance prompt set. - Customer support playbook written for expected complaints (e.g., hallucinations, truncation).
rollout_checklist:
Pre-launch: - Engineering feature-flag implemented and tested (ENG-30112). - Staging telemetry enabled with per-tier dashboards (ENG-30988). - Billing sandbox mapped and verified. - UX copy reviewed by Legal. - Security review completed. - Customer-facing FAQ drafted.

Canary plan: - Day 0: Open admin flag, route 0.1% traffic to Gold and Economy evenly. Monitor for 6 hours. - Step 1: 1% traffic for 24h, evaluate metrics. - Step 2: 5% traffic for 48h, run eval set for quality regressions. - Step 3: 25% traffic for 72h, confirm cost signal and SLA. - Global rollout: ramp to 100% with staged regional expansion and ability to exclude accounts.

Launch day: - Turn on console exposure. - Publish release notes and SDK clients. - Notify enterprise accounts by email with opt-in instructions. - On-call rotations assigned.

Post-launch (30 days): - Weekly quality report for first 4 weeks. - Decide on Economy general availability after objective criteria met. - Execution of scope-reduction plan if regressions discovered.
testing_plan:
Automated tests: - Unit tests for API validation and default behavior. - Integration tests that confirm routing to runtime profiles. - End-to-end bash/pytest harness that simulates prompt mixes and validates billing tags.

Staging experiments: - Inject 10K synthetic requests across prompt length buckets and verify latency P95/P50 per-tier. - Run eval suite of 2K human-label prompts (blind) to measure intent accuracy and hallucination rate across tiers.

Manual QA: - UX smoke test of console flows. - Security sampling verification. - Support readiness checklist walkthrough.

Acceptance gates: - All tests green in staging and synthetic workload targets met for 72 continuous hours. - Quality regression delta <= 3% on core intent metrics for Gold and Standard vs baseline. - Any security or privacy blocking issues resolved.
monitoring_and_sla:
Required signals: error rate (5xx, 4xx), tail latency (P95/P99), token cost per request, user-visible quality metric (automated proxy), circuit-breaker activations. Dashboards: per-tier views for host/region/model. Alerts: - Error rate > 0.5% sustained 5m triggers paging. - P95 latency breach triggers a severity-2 alert. - Quality-proxy regression triggers SRE + PM auto-runbook.

SLA commitments for launch: - Standard: 99.9% availability monthly, latency targets in NFRs. - Gold: elevated availability target with enterprise SLA negotiation required.
migration_and_fallback:
Backward compatibility: omitting 'quality_tier' defaults to Standard. Migration path for customers: - Provide API migration guide with example SDK snippets. - Console bulk-update for routes.

Fallback behavior: - If tier-specific runtime fails, traffic falls back to Standard for that route automatically for the affected region. - Manual rollback instructions in runbook for account-level disable. - Emergency rollback: disable feature-flag globally and restore prior routing configuration.
timeline_and_milestones: Milestone 1 (2025-01-22): API spec and runtime profile definition complete. Milestone 2 (2025-02-05): Runtime routing and telemetry prototype in staging. Milestone 3 (2025-02-19): SDKs and Console UX ready for internal dogfood. Milestone 4 (2025-03-10): Canary start. Milestone 5 (2025-03-21): General availability decision / rollback window close.
